newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, stable week ahead expected.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, stable week ahead expected.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Friday after firming through the week and traders forecast a stable week with mild gains ahead thanks to solid demand.
They predicted few surprise moves in prices of fully-listed Pliva pharmaceuticals and Zagrebacka Banka, which have firmed this week parallel with their GDRs in London.
Some traders said increasing investor interest for food processor Podravka and confectioner Kras could propel their prices up.
"Volume of trading in Kras and Podravka has increased. They are not likely to go down, there is more and more demand," said Josko Milisa of consultancy and brokerage I.F.C.
However, since both firms still had to present their 1995 reports, the market trend might well hinge on those, he added.
* Only one of six traded issues rose, two fell and three were flat.
* The most actively traded Podravka with 6,297 units sold, dipped five kuna during the session but recovered later, closing unchanged at 235 kuna.
* Kras was the only gainer, jumping 25 kuna to 310 to end the week 35 kuna stronger than last Friday. It sold 223 shares.
* Pliva lost 100 kuna to 12,000 on volume of 79 shares.
* Zagrebacka Banka, selling 4,760 shares, flat at 730 kuna.
* Shipper Atlantska Plovidba down to 70 from Wednesday's 80 kuna debut on volume of 77.
* Hotelier Laguna closed flat at 820 kuna with 87 shares traded.
* Volume up at 11,523 units, turnover 6.0 million kuna. Weekly turnover higher at 25.6 million kuna.
